items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'Every child should learn to swim. Swimming is a skill that can save your life if you fall into water. It is also a great way to exercise and have fun with friends.'

What is the author's point? List all the reasons the author gives.
items.answer: The author's point is that every child should learn to swim. The reasons are: (1) swimming can save your life if you fall into water, (2) it is great exercise, and (3) it is fun to do with friends.

steps: Identify the point: every child should learn to swim.
Look for all the supporting reasons.
Reason 1: it can save your life if you fall into water.
Reason 2: it is great exercise.
Reason 3: it is fun to do with friends.
There are three reasons, not just one.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'Having a pet can teach children responsibility. Children must remember to feed their pet and give it fresh water every day. Taking care of a pet helps children learn to think about someone other than themselves.'

Which reason is more important, according to the passage: feeding the pet or learning to think about others? Explain.
items.answer: Learning to think about others is more important according to the passage, because the author frames feeding and watering as examples that lead to the bigger lesson: caring for someone else. The feeding detail supports the bigger idea of responsibility.

steps: The author's point: having a pet teaches responsibility.
Feeding and watering are given as specific examples.
The bigger reason is learning to think about someone other than yourself.
Feeding the pet is a step toward that bigger lesson, not the lesson itself.
The author uses the small task (feeding) to support the big reason (thinking of others).

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'People should spend less time looking at screens. Too much screen time can strain your eyes. It also takes away time that could be spent playing outside or reading books.'

What is the author's point? Does the author give one reason or more than one? List them.
items.answer: The author's point is that people should spend less time on screens. The author gives two reasons: (1) too much screen time can strain your eyes, and (2) it takes away time for playing outside or reading.

steps: Point: people should spend less time on screens.
Look carefully for reasons - there may be more than one.
Reason 1: too much screen time strains your eyes.
Reason 2: it takes away time for playing outside or reading.
The author gives two separate reasons.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'You should always tell the truth. When you tell the truth, people know they can trust you. Lying can hurt your friendships and get you into trouble.'

What reasons does the author give? What is the author trying to convince you to do?
items.answer: The author is trying to convince you to always tell the truth. The reasons are: (1) when you tell the truth, people can trust you, and (2) lying can hurt your friendships and get you in trouble.

steps: Point: always tell the truth.
Reason 1: telling the truth makes people trust you.
Reason 2: lying can hurt friendships.
Reason 3 (part of reason 2): lying can get you into trouble.
All reasons support the author's goal of convincing you to be honest.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'Planting trees is one of the best things we can do for our planet. Trees clean the air by taking in the gas that makes the Earth too warm. They also give shade and homes to many animals.'

The author gives three reasons. Identify each one and explain which you think is the author's STRONGEST reason.
items.answer: The three reasons are: (1) trees clean the air by taking in harmful gases, (2) they give shade, and (3) they give homes to animals. The strongest reason is likely cleaning the air because it helps the whole planet, while shade and animal homes help in more local ways.

steps: Point: planting trees is one of the best things for the planet.
Reason 1: trees clean the air by taking in gases that warm the Earth.
Reason 2: they give shade.
Reason 3: they give homes to many animals.
To find the strongest reason, ask: which one has the biggest impact?
Cleaning the air helps the entire planet, making it the strongest supporting reason.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'Everyone should learn basic first aid. If someone gets hurt, you can help them before a doctor arrives. Knowing first aid can even save a life.'

What point is the author making? Are the two reasons the same or different? Explain.
items.answer: The author's point is that everyone should learn basic first aid. The two reasons are: (1) you can help someone who gets hurt before a doctor arrives, and (2) knowing first aid can save a life. They are related but different: the first is about giving help in any emergency, and the second is about the most serious outcome, saving a life.

steps: Point: everyone should learn basic first aid.
Reason 1: you can help someone before a doctor arrives.
Reason 2: it can save a life.
Are they the same? They are related, but different in strength.
Reason 1 covers everyday emergencies; reason 2 covers the most extreme case.
The author uses both to show a range of how important first aid can be.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'Children should help with chores at home. Doing chores teaches children how to take care of themselves. It also helps the whole family work as a team.'

Is 'helping the family' a good reason to do chores? Does the author explain why? Explain your thinking.
items.answer: Yes, helping the family is a good reason. The author says it helps the family work as a team. This is a reason that benefits others, not just yourself, which makes it a strong supporting point. The author does briefly explain it by saying it involves teamwork.

steps: Point: children should help with chores.
The reason about helping the family: it helps the whole family work as a team.
A team works together, which is a benefit to the group.
The author does explain briefly by connecting chores to teamwork.
This is a valid reason because it shows a benefit beyond just the child.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'Honeybees are very important animals. Without bees, many fruits and vegetables would not grow. Bees pollinate plants, which means they carry pollen so plants can make seeds and fruit.'

The author makes a big claim. What is it? What reason does the author give, and how is that reason explained?
items.answer: The big claim is that honeybees are very important animals. The reason is that without bees, many fruits and vegetables would not grow. The author then explains this reason by saying bees pollinate plants, meaning they carry pollen so plants can make seeds and fruit.

steps: The big claim: honeybees are very important animals.
The main reason: without bees, many fruits and vegetables would not grow.
The author explains WHY by defining pollination.
Pollination means bees carry pollen so plants can make seeds and fruit.
The author first gives the reason, then explains the reason in more detail.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'Students should keep their desks clean and organized. When your desk is organized, you can find your pencils and papers quickly. A messy desk can slow you down and make it hard to focus.'

What are the two reasons the author gives? Are these reasons about helping yourself or helping others?
items.answer: The two reasons are: (1) an organized desk lets you find things quickly, and (2) a messy desk slows you down and makes it hard to focus. Both reasons are about helping yourself, not others. The author is arguing this benefits the student personally.

steps: Point: keep your desk clean and organized.
Reason 1: you can find things quickly.
Reason 2: a messy desk slows you down and hurts your focus.
Ask: who benefits? Both reasons help the student, not others.
The author is making a self-interest argument: being organized helps you.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'You should learn the names of plants in your neighborhood. Knowing plant names helps you enjoy nature more. It also helps you know which plants are safe to touch and which ones to avoid.'

The author gives a practical reason and a safety reason. Identify which is which.
items.answer: The practical reason is that knowing plant names helps you enjoy nature more. The safety reason is that it helps you know which plants are safe to touch and which to avoid.

steps: Point: learn the names of plants in your neighborhood.
Reason 1: knowing names helps you enjoy nature more. This is a practical (everyday benefit) reason.
Reason 2: it helps you know which plants are safe to touch. This is a safety reason.
Practical = makes your life better in a general way.
Safety = protects you from harm.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'Going to the doctor for checkups is very important. A doctor can find problems with your health before they get worse. Regular checkups also keep you up to date on vaccinations.'

Does the author give reasons? How many? Do they both support the same point?
items.answer: Yes, the author gives two reasons. (1) A doctor can find health problems early before they get worse, and (2) checkups keep your vaccinations up to date. Both reasons support the same point: that going to the doctor for checkups is important.

steps: Point: checkups are very important.
Count the reasons: there are two.
Reason 1: a doctor finds problems before they get worse.
Reason 2: checkups keep vaccinations up to date.
Both reasons explain why checkups are important, so both support the same point.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'We should protect sea turtles. Sea turtles have lived on Earth for millions of years. They help keep the ocean healthy by eating jellyfish and sea grass.'

The author gives a historical fact and a scientific reason. Which is which? Which one better supports the argument?
items.answer: The historical fact is that sea turtles have lived on Earth for millions of years. The scientific reason is that they help keep the ocean healthy by eating jellyfish and sea grass. The scientific reason better supports the argument because it explains what sea turtles DO that makes them worth protecting.

steps: Point: we should protect sea turtles.
Reason 1 is historical: turtles have lived for millions of years. It shows they are ancient.
Reason 2 is scientific: they help the ocean by eating jellyfish and sea grass.
Which supports the argument better?
Reason 2 explains why turtles are useful NOW and what we would lose without them.
A scientific reason about current impact is stronger than a historical fact alone.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'Cooking at home is better than always eating out. Home-cooked meals are usually healthier because you control what goes in the food. Cooking at home also costs less money.'

The author gives a health reason and an economic reason. Identify each one. Which do you think the author feels is more important?
items.answer: The health reason is that home-cooked meals are healthier because you control the ingredients. The economic reason is that cooking at home costs less money. Based on the order and the detail given, the author seems to consider the health reason more important since it is listed first and explained more.

steps: Point: cooking at home is better than eating out.
Health reason: home meals are healthier because you control what goes in.
Economic reason: it costs less money.
Which is more important to the author?
The health reason is listed first and gets more explanation.
Authors often put their strongest reason first.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'Firefighters are brave community helpers. They run into burning buildings to rescue people. They also train for many hours each week to stay safe and ready.'

What is the author's point? Do both reasons connect to the idea of firefighters being 'brave'?
items.answer: The author's point is that firefighters are brave community helpers. The first reason (running into burning buildings to rescue people) clearly shows bravery. The second reason (training many hours) shows dedication and preparation, which supports the idea of bravery because it shows they work hard to be able to do brave things.

steps: Point: firefighters are brave community helpers.
Reason 1: they run into burning buildings to rescue people. This is directly about bravery.
Reason 2: they train many hours each week. This shows dedication.
Does training connect to bravery?
Yes: training makes them able to be brave safely; they prepare so they can act bravely.
Both reasons connect to the idea of bravery, though in different ways.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'Singing is good for you. It can lift your mood when you feel sad. Singing also helps you breathe deeply, which is healthy for your lungs.'

The author makes a point about singing. Are the two reasons about feelings, about the body, or both? Explain.
items.answer: The two reasons are about both feelings and the body. Reason 1 is about feelings: singing lifts your mood when you feel sad. Reason 2 is about the body: singing makes you breathe deeply, which is healthy for your lungs. The author supports the point from two different angles: emotional and physical.

steps: Point: singing is good for you.
Reason 1: lifting your mood. This is an emotional/feelings reason.
Reason 2: breathing deeply is healthy for your lungs. This is a physical/body reason.
The author supports the point from two different angles.
This makes the argument stronger because it covers more than one type of benefit.
